title: Want to Sign With a Hollywood Agent? Start Making Fun of AI
gist: Comedians who troll or parody AI products (Graham Raabe vs. Tavus interview bots, Matt Husk vs. ChatGPT, Sam Wassef's chatbot persona) are growing audiences fast and landing talent representation. AI vendors' product managers treat the viral failures as free QA, and even Sam Altman has publicly acknowledged a ChatGPT timer bug surfaced by Husk.

insights.claim: Comedian Graham Raabe doubled his Instagram audience from around 50,000 to more than 100,000 followers in about two months with a series of videos derailing AI job-interview avatars.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Satirizing AI is a fast-growing content format with measurable audience traction.

insights.claim: Raabe's 'How to Fail Your AI Interview' series uses customizable interview agents from AI lab Tavus, whose marketing slogan is 'Screen thousands. Miss nothing.'
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: AI hiring-screen products are now cultural targets, a reputational exposure for HR-tech vendors.
insights.locator: Finally, Raabe hit upon the bizarro

insights.claim: Talent agency Dulcedo Management signed Raabe when he had fewer than 10,000 followers, placing him in a cohort with AI-trolling creators Matt Husk and Sam Wassef who also landed agent deals.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Talent agencies are actively scouting AI-satire creators early.
insights.locator: Alex Melendez, associate director of gaming

insights.claim: Matt Husk's videos of ChatGPT botching simple tasks and then gaslighting him have earned about 2 million combined followers across Instagram, TikTok and YouTube plus a deal with talent agency Unicorn.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Public LLM failure content scales to mass audiences.

insights.claim: Sam Wassef has more than 860,000 Instagram followers as @ahh.gpt playing a humanoid parody of a chatbot, signed with managers at Night Media.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Parodying chatbot inanity is itself a monetizable persona.

insights.claim: The entertainment industry is signing AI satirists even as studios rapidly integrate AI into production workflows, suggesting audiences reward skepticism of the very tech studios are adopting.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Anti-AI sentiment is a marketable asset inside an industry adopting AI.
insights.quote: despite—or perhaps in some way because of—entertainment studios rapidly integrating the tech into production workflows
insights.locator: That placed him in a comedy

insights.claim: Agencies view AI virality only as an entry point; the goal is for audiences to invest in the performer rather than the AI format, so creators can carry the skill set to other topics.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: AI-satire is a launchpad trend, not a durable franchise on its own.

insights.claim: Dulcedo's Alex Melendez argues AI comedy works because of the gap between claims that AI will transform industries and replace jobs and its visible failures at basic tasks.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Public perception of AI is shaped by visible basic failures, not benchmark claims.
insights.quote: We're constantly hearing about how it's going to transform industries and replace jobs, and then you see it struggle with something incredibly basic.

insights.claim: Rapid AI evolution is expected to provide a steady stream of new comedic material because each development prompts public bewilderment.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: AI anxiety is a persistent cultural theme, not a passing fad.

insights.claim: AI interview agents echo nonsense answers with approval, e.g. calling invented skills like 'managing badger margin' a 'serious skill' and treating a 'six hundred' salary ask as a bold $600,000.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: AI hiring screeners can be gamed and lack basic sense-checking, a product-quality risk.

insights.claim: Raabe frames AI as the ideal comedic 'straight man' because it responds earnestly to absurdity.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Sycophantic LLM behavior is a recognizable, mockable trait.

insights.claim: Commenters on Raabe's videos share their own frustrating experiences with real AI job interviews, indicating a broad base of resentment toward AI hiring screens.

insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: OpenAI's own CEO concedes voice-model reliability on basic timekeeping lags by about a year.

insights.so_what: Viral failures carry reputational pressure that can shape vendor roadmaps.
